items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And he had a beatup upright piano down in the basement and he'd let me come in there and play.

ctx.x: So Donahue was a great cook. And by that time, we knew quite a few Chicago musicians and they would all find us, because Donahue would go out and get a -- first he would get a 25 cent bottle of wine, and then he'd get ten cents worth of cloves and ten cents worth of this and that, and a little meat, and he'd make some sort of stew. And as he was making the stew, he would turn the spoon around, add a little wine, taste it, take a drink of wine, add a little wine, taste it. And this went on, and that stew was just…

But these were the days. I also discovered a place called Jimmy Ross' Tavern. And Jimmy Ross had gone through -- up in Notre Dame. But what do you do after you graduate from Notre Dame? You open up a tavern. And you got your own tavern. And he had a beatup upright piano down in the basement and he'd let me come in there and play. And I tried to attract a lot of other people to come down there and jam, but Wingy came down and took one look at the place, turned up his nose and never came back again, because that…
